notes: Lexemes: the 25 of chapters.json proposed_for_frozen_rows.3 (adopted at plan-revise P001) plus the place chunk í heyinu, 26 in new_lexeme_ids (ceiling 27). Incidental verbs first used here: sér, les, á (3sg only, not counted in the budget). hefur (hafa) was moved to Kafli 4 s012 („Hann hefur ekki átta fætur!“, of a horse that is not Sleipnir) at fix 20261027T031328857-is-kvold-01-fix (F002), because no aid from known words could carry it at s048. The checker's advisory grammar-unlicensed warning for heyinu now also fires at s048, as at s047, s049 and s056: í heyinu is the row's place chunk, not yet in course.json.place_chunks (the runner's).
G03 in the first third: menn, konur, börn (s004–s006), Ásta counts the people (s008). Every plural is a nominative subject or predicate; no third-person plural verb except eru (G04).
Beat 3's „under a haycock“ is told as „í heyinu“ (the supplement's place chunk): undir is Kafli 11. The haycock is a small one at the edge of the field that nobody counted (s045).

„Everyone carries hay“ without bera (not licensed): Óli kemur og fer, kemur og fer, og heyið fer líka (s028); Óli, the women, the men and the horses are fljót (s029–s033); Ásta counts the haycocks down (s035); Þar er hlaðan, og nú er heyið þar (s037). Codex review: hefur hey for carrying was dropped as an English workaround.

Hook: afi owns the book (s057–s058; first-use support for á: the margin diagram is-kvold-01-l03-svg-eiga at s057, closing IS03-02). Bjarni keeps it: he leaves with it at s053 and again after his s060 refusal, explicitly staged at s061. Afi and Siggi then sit together without the book (s063). Only the supported á bók is used; no new accusative or genitive paradigm.
Objects whose form equals the nominative (supported, logged): sér skýið (s025), á bók (s057, s058). No other objects.

12 margin glosses, none of the define kind: the define gloss for fljótur was dropped at the Codex review (coming and going is not quickness); fljótur rests on the race context. Kindurnar … hvítar (s016) adds a third use of hvítur and a feminine plural. Bjarni's line Blautt gras er ekki hey was cut as untrue (hay can be wet); s034 Hlaðan er stór was folded into s037 so that þar is anchored; s034 and s041 are retired ids.

Media: margin_vignette 0 (Hluti 1 expects 4–10, a checker warning): the two SVGs carry the concrete nouns (hey, hrífa, sáta, hlaða, gras, heiði, sól, ský, rigning), so raster vignettes would duplicate them. The planned cover and two scenes support but never carry meaning.
Orð með sögu uses heyannir only as the headword, explained in its own lines; it is not a story token.

cover.alt: Haymaking on the sunny home field of Hamrar: five adults rake and gather hay; Siggi holds a rake, Ásta counts on her fingers beside seated afi, and Snati lies at afi's feet. Four Icelandic horses stand side by side by the turf hay barn, two large ones with pack frames and two small ones; white clouds hang over the heath.
cover.art_brief: A sunny afternoon in late August 1874, warm light and small white clouds over the home field of Hamrar in Jökuldalur. Keep the established Kafli 1–2 ink-and-watercolour farm setting: three dark tarred timber gables with white trim, turf walls and grass roofs; the long low turf hay barn beside the farmhouse; brown-green heath and the two-banded basalt crag behind. Pale drying hay lies in rows with several round haycocks, and a strip of standing green grass remains at the field edge. Five adult workers form one clear group: Bjarni and Óli rake with long wooden hay rakes, while Guðrún, Helga and Þórunn rake and gather hay. Four Icelandic horses stand beside the barn, fully in frame and separated by visible gaps, all on the same level and at the same distance from the viewer: exactly two large horses and two smaller horses, with pack frames. Each horse has one separate head, body and four legs; their size contrast is clear without perspective tricks. Foreground right: Ásta counts on her fingers beside afi, seated on his flat stone with his stick; Snati lies at his feet. Foreground left: Siggi stands holding his rake and looks toward the farmhouse. Keep all eight people distinct and countable: Bjarni 44, broad and dark-bearded; Óli 24, the tallest, red-cheeked and red-bearded, cap and plain cream work jumper; Guðrún 38, dark peysuföt and small black skotthúfa; Helga 18, tall, honey-brown plaits and dark working dress; Þórunn 36, thin, brown shawl and grey apron; Siggi 11, thin, tousled sandy hair, plain brown knitted work jumper, grey breeches and sewn sheepskin shoes on both feet; Ásta 6, white-blond plaits, dark-red mid-calf dress and white apron; afi 73, white hair and chin-beard, dark-blue jacket, dark knitted cap and stick. Snati is the cream-and-tan Icelandic sheepdog with pointed ears and curled tail. Plain period work clothes, simple knitting. No text, letters or numerals anywhere.

inference_aids.art_brief: Late afternoon in late August 1874 on the home field of Hamrar. Heavy black clouds fill the sky and darken the heath: dim overcast light over the whole field, with no sunlight and no rain yet falling on the workers or hay. Óli, the tall red-bearded farmhand in a cap and plain cream work jumper, hurries toward the open door of the long low turf hay barn with a huge armful of hay. Bjarni, broad and dark-bearded in plain work clothes, leads an Icelandic horse carrying two balanced bundles of hay toward the same door. Helga, tall with honey-brown plaits and a dark working dress, and thin Þórunn in a brown shawl and grey apron, rake hay into heaps with long wooden hay rakes; Guðrún, in dark peysuföt and a small black skotthúfa, gathers a bundle. Haycocks remain clearly visible beyond them. In the foreground Ásta, six, white-blond plaits, dark-red mid-calf dress and white apron, hurries with a small armful of hay; Snati, the cream-and-tan Icelandic sheepdog with a curled tail, runs beside her. Show only these six people and the dog. Separate their silhouettes and let the forward lean of the running figures make their speed clear. Established Kafli 1–2 farm ink-and-watercolour style; turf-and-stone walls and grass roof, simple wooden tools, plain period work clothes. No text, letters or numerals anywhere.

inference_aids.art_brief: Minutes later on the same day at Hamrar, heavy rain falls in grey slanting lines and the daylight is dim blue-grey. At the edge of the mown home field, beside the turf wall, stands one small haycock; a wooden hay rake lies on the ground beside it. Wet Snati, the cream-and-tan Icelandic sheepdog with pointed ears and curled tail, stands barking at the haycock. Bjarni, 44, broad and dark-bearded, in soaked plain work clothes and a dripping hat, has pulled the hay aside with one hand and looks down in astonishment. Inside the hollow in the hay, Siggi, 11, thin, tousled sandy hair, plain brown knitted work jumper, grey breeches and sewn sheepskin shoes on both healed feet, lies on his stomach reading an open thick calfskin-backed paper manuscript. His gaze and one finger follow a row of loose wavy ink strokes, his lips parted as he reads aloud; the page marks contain no letters or recognisable symbols. The book is large enough to recognise and rain-spotted pages are clear. Keep Bjarni, Siggi, Snati, the wet hay and the dropped rake as the focus, with the established dark tarred farmhouse gables and low turf hay barn small and dim behind. Established Kafli 1–2 farm ink-and-watercolour style. No text, letters or numerals anywhere.

words_with_history.title: Orð með sögu
text: Heyannir: sumar, sól, mikið hey og mikið fólk á túninu.
words_with_history.note_en: Heyannir ('hay-toils') was a month of the old Icelandic calendar, from late July to late August, named for the haymaking that filled it; the next month began in the last week of August. Hey is the same word as English hay. Hay brought in wet could rot, so a black cloud sent everyone running.

grammar.title: barn → börn
grammar.rule: hestur → hestar → hestarnir · maður → menn → mennirnir · hrífa → hrífur → hrífurnar · ský → ský → skýin · barn → börn → börnin

tables.caption: er · eru
rows: Nú eru skýin mörg og svört.

grammar.note_en: Patterns in this chapter: hestur → hestar → hestarnir; kona → konur; hrífa → hrífurnar; ský → ský → skýin; barn → börn → börnin. Maður → menn → mennirnir is irregular: learn it whole. The plural takes eru: Óli er fljótur "Óli is quick", Mennirnir eru fljótir "The men are quick", Siggi og Ásta eru börn "Siggi and Ásta are children"; fólk is singular (fólkið er). Adjectives agree: fljótir (kk. ft.), fljótar (kvk. ft.), fljót (hk. ft.). In some forms a alternates with ö: barn → börn, saga → sögur, svart → svört. This does not happen before every written u (svartur, strákur). Abbreviations: et. singular, ft. plural; kk. masculine, kvk. feminine, hk. neuter.

items.prompt: Hér er bók. ___ er blaut. (hann / hún / það)
Snati er hundur, en Ásta er lítil ___. (st…)
Í dag er ekki sól. Skýin eru svört, og ___ kemur. (ri…)
Óli kemur og fer, kemur og fer. Hann er ___. (fl…)
Óli er blautur, en hlaðan er ekki blaut. Hún er ___.
Nú er ekki rigning. Nú er ___, og heyið er þurrt. (só…)
Afi, Bjarni, Guðrún, Helga, Siggi og Ásta: hér er mikið ___.
Þetta er ekki bær. Þetta er ___, og heyið er þar. (hl…)
Það er sól. Hvar er fólkið?
model_answers: Það er á túninu, á Jökuldal.
items.rubric: On the home field (á túninu), raking hay. Any sentence that puts the people on the tún is right.

items.prompt: Bjarni og Óli eru menn, og Guðrún, Helga og Þórunn eru konur. En Siggi og Ásta?
model_answers: Þau eru tvö börn. Siggi er strákur, og Ásta er stelpa.
items.rubric: They are children (börn: barn → börn); Siggi is a boy (strákur), Ásta a girl (stelpa). Either order of the names, a pronoun or the names are all fine.

items.prompt: Hvað sér Helga, og hvað segir Bjarni?
items.model_answer: Helga sér svart ský. Bjarni segir: „Það kemur rigning!“
model_answers: Helga sér svart ský. Bjarni segir: „Það kemur rigning!“
Hún sér ský, stórt og svart. Bjarni segir: „Það kemur rigning, og heyið er á túninu!“
items.rubric: Helga sees a big black cloud over the heath; Bjarni says rain is coming and the hay is still on the home field.

items.model_answer: Það kemur rigning, og heyið er á túninu.
model_answers: Það kemur rigning, og heyið er á túninu.
Skýið er stórt og svart, og það kemur rigning. Heyið er þurrt, og það er á túninu.
items.rubric: Rain is coming and the dry hay is still out on the field; the hay must be in the barn before it gets wet, so everyone hurries.

items.prompt: Hvar liggur Siggi, og hvað les hann?
items.model_answer: Siggi liggur í heyinu, og hann les bók.
model_answers: Siggi liggur í heyinu, og hann les bók.
Hann er á túninu. Hann liggur í heyinu og les.
items.rubric: In a small haycock at the edge of the home field (í heyinu, á túninu), reading afi's book instead of working.

items.prompt: En þú? Hvað er hér í dag: sól, rigning, ský?
items.model_answer: Í dag er sól, og skýin eru hvít.
model_answers: Í dag er sól, og skýin eru hvít.
Í dag er ekki sól. Rigningin er mikil, og skýin eru mörg og svört.
items.rubric: Answer in a full sentence, not just já or nei: any true answer about today's weather in the frame Í dag er …; if you mention the clouds, make the adjective plural (hvít, svört, mörg).
